questions.q: What is the sole patching mechanism for SQL Server 2017 and later?
options: Cumulative Updates (CUs) — Service Packs were phased out after SQL Server 2016
Service Packs, released quarterly
GDR builds are the only mechanism for any supported version
Manual binary replacement with no official update packages
questions.explain: Service Packs ended after SQL Server 2016. CUs are cumulative and are the entire patching lifecycle for 2017 and later.

questions.q: What does it mean that Cumulative Updates are 'cumulative'?
options: A later CU contains everything earlier CUs for that version contained, so you never need to install a chain of updates to catch up
Each CU only contains the single fix released that month
CUs accumulate configuration changes that must be manually merged
Cumulative refers to combining CUs from different major versions
questions.explain: Installing the latest CU brings you fully current — CU12 includes everything in CU1 through CU11 plus more.

questions.q: Which function returns structured, scriptable build information (like ProductVersion and CU level), as opposed to a single human-readable string?
options: SERVERPROPERTY()
@@VERSION only
sp_helpdb
DBCC CHECKDB
questions.explain: SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion'), ('ProductLevel'), and ('ProductUpdateLevel') return structured values you can script against; @@VERSION returns one string.

questions.q: Per this lesson's recommended cadence, where should a new CU be applied first?
options: Test/staging environments, never production first
Production, immediately upon release
Whichever environment is most convenient that week
It doesn't matter, since CUs carry no risk
questions.explain: New CUs should always go to test/staging first with a soak period before production, even though CUs are generally lower-risk than major version upgrades.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against letting a supported instance drift far behind the current CU?
options: Falling far behind turns future patching into a bigger, riskier jump and leaves known published vulnerabilities unpatched longer
Old CUs stop being cumulative after six months
SQL Server automatically uninstalls itself if too far behind
Drifting behind has no real consequence as long as backups exist
questions.explain: Staying within a CU or two of current keeps each patch small and keeps known security fixes applied in a timely way.
